summary: Black Hills lookout: CCC tower of 1938 replaced by a 54-ft steel tower in 1960 after Sundance AFS construction; staffed in fire season, drive-up, NHLR-registered 2026.

facts.design: 54-ft steel tower and cab (1960); original 1938 cab was L-4

access.note: Reached by a short dirt road signed for the lookout, off Warren Peak Road. Stairs can be climbed almost to the top; the top floor is locked.

visit.trail_note: Short dirt road from Warren Peak Road, free parking at the base. Stairs reach almost to the top; the top floor is locked (Hiking Project).

events.note: Original ten-foot tower with a live-in cab, built by the Civilian Conservation Corps. firelookout.com calls the cab an enclosed L-4 cab, dated 1938-1939.
Original tower demolished during construction of the Sundance Air Force Station.
Steel tower and cab placed a short distance east of the original. 54 ft per Forest Service and Wikipedia; 53 ft per firelookout.com. NHLR gives 1960 as the build year.

corrections.proposed: 54-ft steel tower and cab (1960); original 1938 cab was L-4
corrections.why: firelookout.com describes the L-4 cab for the original 1938-1939 lookout. The Forest Service describes the standing 1960 structure as a 54-foot steel tower and cab, with no L-4 designation.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1960 tower is 54 feet per the Forest Service and Wikipedia, and 53 feet per firelookout.com. The record and story use 54 feet and note the disagreement.
NHLR gives 1960 as the build year. The Forest Service and Wikipedia give 1938 for the original lookout and 1960 for the replacement. The story gives both dates.
Hiking Project mentions a pit toilet at the base. The Forest Service says restroom information is not available. The story reports both.

notes_for_editor: History is well sourced across the Forest Service, NHLR and Wikipedia. Access and restroom details rest on Hiking Project, a third-party listing that may be out of date. The brief's design L-4 most likely describes the 1938 cab, so it is corrected. The first lookout's name is unresolved: NHLR says Mert Ellsbury, firelookout.com says Lyman Ellsbury for 1939. The story reports both. Staffing source is NHLR undated text, so as_of is undated. Brief elevation 2028.7 m matches NHLR 6,656 ft; Wikipedia says 6,640 ft. Sundance AFS radar claim is from the Forest Service page and was not separately checked. No photos added.
